mission: Gray Swan is an AI security company founded by researchers behind well-known jailbreak and defence work. It runs the Arena, a large public red-teaming network, pre-release adversarial evaluations for frontier labs, and sells Shade (automated attack testing) and Cygnal (runtime filtering of adversarial inputs and unsafe agent outputs).

key_work.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models (GCG)
key_work.plain_summary: Founders' CMU research: automatically found text suffixes that jailbreak many chatbots at once, showing safety training is brittle.

key_work.title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
key_work.plain_summary: Interrupts the model's internal representations of harmful outputs, making it far harder to jailbreak.

key_work.title: Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment: Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition
key_work.plain_summary: A huge public red-teaming contest (with UK AISI) found that nearly every AI agent tested could be made to break its rules.

key_work.title: Gray Swan Arena
key_work.plain_summary: What Gray Swan calls the world's largest adversarial red-teaming network, with more than 15,000 researchers attacking models.

key_work.title: Cygnal
key_work.plain_summary: Runtime filter that blocks adversarial inputs and unsafe agent outputs.

people.role: Co-founder and chief scientist (also CMU professor and OpenAI board member)

warnings.text: AI agents with real access can be compromised without anyone noticing.
Defences tested only against known attacks miss new ones.

recommendations.text: Test against attacks discovered by large adversarial communities, not just known ones.
Enforce agent behaviour at runtime, not only before deployment.
